description: We are students from Colegio Nuestra Señora del Luján in Montevideo, Uruguay. We love researching space, programming, and building models. We are very enthusiastic about space and learning new things. This is our first time participating in a hackathon, and we are very excited about this experience!
summary:
Project Summary – Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer
We created an interactive space station model using recycled materials, featuring LED lights, gears, and a control panel. Our project also includes a solar panel connected to a Makey Makey board to control a video game about collecting space debris, a hydraulic elevator that demonstrates Pascal's Principle, and a LEGO astronaut.
Our mission trainer combines science, engineering, robotics, and programming to simulate different aspects of space exploration. It is designed to help children understand how space technology works, discover the challenges astronauts face, and learn about the importance of keeping space clean.
This educational prototype could inspire future generations of astronauts and help NASA bring space exploration closer to young learners through hands-on activities, creativity, and interactive learning.
details:
Our project is an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer designed to help children explore space through science, engineering, and technology.

We built a space station using recycled materials, with LED lights, gears, and a control panel. We also created a hydraulic elevator using syringes, tubes, and water to demonstrate Pascal's Principle. A solar panel connected to a Makey Makey board works as a controller for our video game, where players must click on pieces of space debris to collect them and complete the mission within 60 seconds. We also built an astronaut using LEGO bricks.

We used recycled materials, LEGO, Makey Makey, LEDs, hydraulic components, and Scratch to develop our project and video game.

Our project combines hands-on experiments, robotics, and interactive gaming to make learning fun. It encourages creativity, teamwork, problem-solving, and environmental awareness while inspiring children to learn about space exploration and imagine themselves as future astronauts.
